title: fix(cuda-graphs): resolve warmup regression with shape guards during capture/replay
author: Miguel Torres
description:
Context: A warmup regression was observed when using CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards enabled. This regression surfaced as increased cold-start latency and occasional incorrect KV-cache priming for variable sequence lengths after the changes in pr-22345 and follow-ups (see related PRs).
Motivation: restore prior warmup behavior while keeping shape-guard based safe-capture semantics so capture/replay works for mixed-length workloads.
Summary of changes: - Ensure the shape-guard prologue (shape checks + guard activation) is executed before the first graph capture pass so that the captured graph includes the guard path. - Add explicit dim/stride stabilization for transient tensors used in KV cache priming to avoid non-deterministic kernel selection during replay. - Move warmup token generation to a dedicated non-captured path that still populates KV cache but does not cause graph divergence for later captures. - Add unit/integration tests that simulate mixed-length batches and replay scenarios, plus a perf harness to measure cold-starts.
Checklist: - [x] Reproduce regression with minimal test-case - [x] Add fix ensuring prologue runs before capture - [x] Add tests covering mixed-length replay - [x] Address flaky CI by increasing deterministic seeding for memory allocators - [x] Run perf lab benchmarks on p3 and a100 - [x] Add release notes and changelog entry
Tests & CI: - Local reproduce: Added reproducer in tests/runtime/test_cuda_graph_warmup.py that failed on HEAD and passes with this branch. - CI: initial CI run failed (gpu-integration test timed out on replay harness). Root cause was a race in the test harness; fixed by a small synchronization in tests/util/replay_harness.py and re-ran. Final CI status: all checks passed (linux-build, unit, gpu-integration, perf-canary).
Commits: - "Fix: run shape-guard prologue before cudaGraph capture (torres)" - "Stabilize transient KV tensor dims/strides before kernel selection" - "Move warmup token generation to non-captured priming path" - "tests: add mixed-length replay reproducer + smoke perf check" - "ci: increase determinism in replay harness to avoid flakiness"
Files changed (high-level): - runtime/cuda/cuda_graph_manager.cpp (core capture/replay ordering, ~+210 -45) - runtime/cuda/shape_guard.cpp (prologue invocation and guard lifecycle) - runtime/kv_cache/kv_priming.cpp (stabilize tensor metadata during priming) - tests/runtime/test_cuda_graph_warmup.py (new) - tests/util/replay_harness.py (test synchronization fix) - perf/bench/cuda_graph_cold_start.py (benchmark) - docs/notes/cuda-graph-warmup.md (explain regression and mitigation)
Impact & rationale: - The regression increased median cold-start by ~35% in our perf-canary for mixed-length workloads. By ensuring the prologue runs before a capture, captured graphs represent the guarded execution path and therefore replay is stable across subsequent replays with different sequence lengths. - Stabilizing transient tensor metadata prevents the runtime from picking divergent kernels between capture and replay which caused incorrect priming of the KV cache.
Observability & rollout: - Added a conf flag runtime.cuda_graph.shape_guard.prologue_first (default true) to allow telemetry-assisted rollouts. - Added metrics: cuda_graph.warmup.latency and cuda_graph.replay.mismatch_rate to the perf dashboard.
Related work / references: related PRs pr-22345, pr-22256, pr-21810; Linear tasks ENG-1589 ENG-1620. Merge: squashed and merged to main after approvals and green CI.

release_notes: Fixes a warmup regression when using CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards: ensures prologue runs before capture and stabilizes transient tensor metadata to prevent kernel selection divergence. Adds metrics for warmup latency and replay mismatch rate.
